name: Trail2D
shortDescription: Add 2D trails, with up to 2 colors and gradients, following any object.
description: **Adds 2D trail objects that follow another object as it moves.**
Customize the trail appearance with up to 2 colors, blended together as a gradient.
1. Add a Trail2D object to your scene, depending on your game's dimension.
2. Configure the trail's colors and gradient in the object's properties.
3. Use the object's actions to attach it to the object you want to leave a trail behind.

eventsFunctions.description: the start tint of the object. Tint applied at the head of the trail (the object's current position), multiplied with the texture below (if any).
eventsFunctions.name: StartColor

eventsFunctions.description: the start opacity of the object. Opacity (0-255) of the trail at the head.
eventsFunctions.name: StartOpacity

eventsFunctions.description: the end tint of the object. Tint applied at the tail of the trail (its oldest point), multiplied with the texture below (if any).
eventsFunctions.name: EndColor

eventsFunctions.description: the end opacity of the object. Opacity (0-255) of the trail at the tail.
eventsFunctions.name: EndOpacity

eventsFunctions.description: the head width of the object. Thickness of the trail at the object's current position (the head), in pixels.
eventsFunctions.name: Width

eventsFunctions.description: the tail width of the object. Thickness of the trail at its oldest point (the tail), in pixels. Use a different value than the head width to make the trail taper.
eventsFunctions.name: TailWidth

eventsFunctions.description: the points count of the object. Number of points used to draw the trail (higher values make a longer, smoother trail but cost more performance).
eventsFunctions.name: PointsCount

eventsFunctions.description: the point spacing of the object. Distance (in pixels) represented by each point of the trail. Used to smooth out fast movements (e.g. on a slower computer) by adding several points at once instead of one, so the trail keeps the same density regardless of the framerate.
